data.title: PR-15 IMPL-04: declared unsupported cases for time/network/process/storage packs; profiles 0.2.0

data.body: [HIGH] Stable profile names bypass protected-intent revision. This change keeps PROFILE_NAME at network/adversarial-v0 while lines 41-48 add assumptions and bump only the internal version. The process and storage profiles do the same. The contract stores profiles as bare names, and crates/continuum-intent/src/faults.rs:386-397 checks only membership in BTreeSet<String>; crates/continuum-intent/src/contract.rs:1797-1819 supplies no version or fingerprint. Therefore the existing protected Intent Contract can resolve the same names while the profiles admit fewer environments. ADR-0039:7-16 and RFC-0031:153-155 require strengthened assumptions to use a semantic diff and policy authorization. RFC-0027:507 also requires content-addressed profile pinning. The profile fingerprints and version bumps are counterevidence only inside each pack; no contract or snapshot binding consumes them. Required fix: bind each referenced profile to immutable content identity, or at least version plus fingerprint, fail closed on drift, and require revise-intent authorization for changed assumptions. Risk-high answers: (1) Failure modes: same-name drift silently strengthens assumptions, reuses intent identity, and can yield false-positive success evidence. (2) Edge cases: same version with changed bytes, changed version with the same name, missing packs, old artifacts, and composed profiles must all fail closed. (3) Rollback: restore the 0.1.0 semantics or publish immutable new profile identities, then invalidate and recompute affected evidence. (4) Monitoring: reject and alert on profile digest drift and on evidence whose intent omits bound pack identities. (5) Input validation: require exact signed profile identity at contract acceptance and prove with negative tests that any mismatch needs an authorized intent revision.

[MEDIUM] Service-discovery failures are not covered by network-no-forgery. Lines 524-529 say stale discovery may route an envelope to the wrong node, but assign Reliance::Assumed(network-no-forgery). That assumption at lines 334-338 only says a delivered envelope was sent to its receiver with unchanged sender and payload. An envelope can be sent to a stale, incorrect receiver and still satisfy that statement. The machine-readable reliance therefore omits the actual prerequisite for excluding discovery faults. Add a distinct fixed-addressing or correct-discovery assumption, or classify this behavior as OutsidePack. Add a negative test with stale resolution to prove the selected reliance excludes the stated behavior; the existing table-equality test only pins the current mismatch.

data.reason: HIGH: profile assumption changes retain stable names, while Intent Contracts resolve only names. This bypasses protected-intent semantic diff and authorization. MEDIUM: service-discovery faults rely on network-no-forgery, which does not exclude stale or wrong resolution.

data.body: [RESOLVED][HIGH] The target now preserves network/adversarial-v0 as a separate frozen profile and publishes changed content as network/adversarial-v1 (crates/continuum-effects-network/src/profile.rs:36-42,661-687). The registry pins both canonical fingerprints (crates/continuum-effects-network/tests/pr15_impl04_unsupported.rs:693-735). Intent adoption uses a named revision: an undeclared v1 fails W8, replacing v0 is blocked, and trust adoption fails closed to review (crates/continuum-semantic-diff/tests/pr15_impl04_profile_revision.rs:236-255,257-297,319-357). Risk-high answers: (1) Failure modes: same-name drift could reuse intent identity and certify stronger assumptions, but frozen v0 plus new v1 identities prevents that drift. (2) Edge cases: missing, unknown, replaced, or trust-promoted profiles fail closed; both v0 and v1 remain distinct. (3) Rollback: contracts keep v0, so rollback selects the frozen identity and discards v1-derived evidence. (4) Monitoring: the registry fingerprint tests expose any same-name byte drift, while W8 exposes undeclared identities. (5) Input validation: exact declared names are checked at contract acceptance, and revise-intent authorization remains required for acceptance. The risk:critical human gate remains separate.

[RESOLVED][MEDIUM] ServiceDiscovery now relies on fixed-addressing, whose statement excludes late, stale, wrong, and missing resolution (crates/continuum-effects-network/src/profile.rs:374-378,550-556). The negative stale-resolution test proves network-no-forgery still holds while the machine-readable reliance selects fixed-addressing (crates/continuum-effects-network/tests/pr15_impl04_unsupported.rs:653-691).

data.reason: Reviewed the whole persisted range through ca6b59714c0ecca6ec4693e4ef33cf9b3fbd0381. The immutable profile-identity and fixed-addressing repairs resolve the open security findings. No remaining security blocker. This vote does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.
